# Terminology

**Generated by `task docs` from [`terminology.yaml`](terminology.yaml). Do not edit.**

Each record names one concept in one context: what it is, how it relates to
other concepts, the identifiers that spell it, and the words to write instead
of it. A word with two meanings in two contexts is two records. `spec.md`
stays normative: a record quotes the specification and may not disagree with
it. `task check:terms` holds the records, the schemas and the prose together,
and the words to avoid are enforced in prose by the generated
`MusherSpecifications` Vale style.

206 record(s). A record marked *proposed* is an open item, not yet a decision.

## Concept system

Each concept under the whole it is part of, with the concept it is a kind of
in brackets. A concept that is part of two wholes appears under both.

```text
blueprint [blueprint.blueprint] (a kind of core.musher-document)
  - deployment parameter [blueprint.deployment-parameter]
    - parameter from [blueprint.parameter-from]
    - parameter origin [blueprint.parameter-origin] (a kind of blueprint.origin)
  - item revision [blueprint.item-revision]
  - node [blueprint.node]
    - binding [blueprint.binding]
    - compute [blueprint.compute]
      - compute profile [blueprint.compute-profile]
        - compute family [blueprint.compute-family]
        - compute size [blueprint.compute-size]
        - compute tier [blueprint.compute-tier]
      - placement constraint [blueprint.placement-constraint]
    - document reference [blueprint.document-reference]
    - exposure [blueprint.exposure]
      - access [blueprint.access]
      - access exemption [blueprint.access-exemption]
      - viewer claim [blueprint.viewer-claim]
      - viewer identity mode [blueprint.viewer-identity-mode]
      - visibility [blueprint.visibility]
    - volume allocation [blueprint.volume-allocation]
      - storage class [blueprint.storage-class]
  - node graph [blueprint.node-graph]
    - value dependency [blueprint.value-dependency]

catalog [catalog.catalog]
  - catalog item [catalog.catalog-item]
    - item document [core.item-document] (a kind of core.musher-document)
    - item root [core.item-root]
    - listing [listing.listing] (a kind of core.musher-document)
      - category [listing.category]
      - display name [listing.display-name]

      - icon [listing.icon]

      - license [listing.license]
      - lifecycle stage [listing.lifecycle-stage]
      - listing URL [listing.listing-url]
      - media path [listing.media-path]
      - overview [listing.overview]
        - overview Markdown profile [listing.overview-markdown-profile]
      - published media set [listing.published-media-set]
      - screenshot [listing.screenshot]
      - summary [listing.summary]
      - tag [listing.tag]

component [component.component] (a kind of core.musher-document)
  - component contract [component.component-contract]
    - input [component.input]
    - output [component.output]
      - output origin [component.output-origin]
  - component type [component.type]
  - workload [component.workload]
    - build recipe [component.build-recipe]
      - build argument [component.build-argument]
      - build context [component.build-context]
      - build secret [component.build-secret]
    - command [component.command]
    - endpoint [component.endpoint]
      - endpoint path [component.endpoint-path]
      - endpoint property [component.endpoint-property]

      - OIDC client [component.oidc-client]
      - target port [component.target-port]
      - trust policy [component.trust-policy]
    - probe [component.probe]
      - probe credential [component.probe-credential]
    - schedule [component.schedule]
    - source [component.source]
      - source content key [component.source-content-key]
      - source root [component.source-root]
    - volume [component.volume]

conformance corpus [repository.conformance-corpus]
  - behaviour suite [repository.behaviour-suite]
  - conformance case [repository.conformance-case]

connection [blueprint.connection]
  - connection member [component.connection-member]

connection input [component.connection-input] (a kind of component.input)
  - connection capability [component.connection-capability]

core [core.core] (a kind of core.family)
  - what a family fixes [core.family-parameter]
  - what belongs in core [core.membership-test]

deployment [deployment.deployment]
  - deployment snapshot [deployment.deployment-snapshot]
    - allocation [deployment.allocation]
    - deployment fact [deployment.deployment-fact]
    - selection [blueprint.selection]
      - selection kind [blueprint.selection-kind]
      - view [blueprint.view]
  - replica [deployment.replica]
  - resolution [deployment.resolution]
    - resolution record [deployment.resolution-record]
      - artifact digest [deployment.artifact-digest]
      - specification releases [deployment.specification-releases]
    - stage [deployment.resolution-stage]
  - rollout [deployment.rollout]

diagnostic [core.diagnostic]
  - diagnostic code [core.diagnostic-code]

Musher document [core.musher-document] (a kind of core.yaml-document)
  - envelope [core.envelope]
    - kind [core.kind]
    - metadata [core.metadata]
      - component revision [component.revision]
      - slug [core.slug]

placeholder [core.placeholder]
  - namespace [core.placeholder-namespace]
  - placeholder grammar [core.placeholder-grammar]

publication [catalog.publication]
  - publication obligation [catalog.publication-obligation]

validation scope [core.validation-scope]

value input [component.value-input] (a kind of component.input)
```

## Terms by context

### Core: what every document shares

#### <a id="core-admission-phase"></a>admission phase

The validation phase run by the publisher or the platform, for obligations that
need the catalog, an account or a policy, such as a revision that increases or a
description present at publication.

- **Kind of:** [validation phase](#core-validation-phase)
- **Avoid:** "capability" (banned, identifier): write "admission". The phase
  value and the case-tree directory.
- **Avoid:** "capability phase" (banned, prose): write "admission phase".
- **Avoid:** "capability check" (banned, prose): write "admission check".
- **Avoid:** "capability checks" (banned, prose): write "admission checks".
- **Source:** [core v2 §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers),
  [ADR 0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-core"></a>core

The base family: the specification that defines no kind and states the envelope,
compatibility, item, grammar, phase and shared-diagnostic rules every other
family applies.

- **Kind of:** [family](#core-family)
- **Source:** [core v2 §1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#scope), [ADR
  0022](adr/0022-the-musher-document-core-specification.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-core-release"></a>core release

One tagged release of the base family, which each release of another family
records as the one it was built and tested against.

- **Kind of:** [release](#repository-release)
- **Verbs:** a family release records its core release; every core release
  re-releases its dependent families
- **Not to be confused with:** Protobuf and Rust editions, which are semantics
  epochs, not releases.
- **Avoid:** "edition" (banned, prose): write "core release".
- **Avoid:** "editions" (banned, prose): write "core releases".
- **Avoid:** "dependency editions" (banned, prose): write "dependency releases".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §9](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#editions), [ADR
  0023](adr/0023-published-bytes-are-immutable-release-assets.md), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: versioning, publication.

#### <a id="core-deferred-obligation"></a>deferred obligation

A rule a validator could not decide for lack of context, reported with its
requirement, its document pointer and the missing context, and making the result
INCOMPLETE.

- **Part of:** [validation scope](#core-validation-scope)
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §6.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#coverage)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-diagnostic"></a>diagnostic

One reported failure of a document: a normative code, the phase that found it, a
JSON Pointer path into the submitted document, and non-normative message text.

- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_FIELD`
- **Verbs:** a diagnostic anchors at a path; an implementation reports a
  diagnostic
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §7](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#diagnostics)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-diagnostic-code"></a>diagnostic code

The stable ERR_ name of one condition a document can fail, declared in exactly
one diagnostics table with every phase it may be reported in.

- **Part of:** [diagnostic](#core-diagnostic)
- **Source:** [core v2 §7](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#diagnostics)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-diagnostic-registry"></a>diagnostic registry

The set of diagnostic codes a family's documents may be reported with: the
family's own diagnostics table, core's, and those of the families it declares as
normative dependencies, each code with every phase that may report it.

- **lists:** [diagnostic code](#core-diagnostic-code)
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#bindings), [core
  v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §7](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#diagnostics)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-dns-label-grammar"></a>DNS-label grammar

The identifier grammar `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9]$`, two to sixty-three
characters, for a name composed into a host name or materialized under its own
name.

- **Identifiers:** grammars: `dns-label`
- **Example:** A slug, a node name and a component volume name take the
  DNS-label grammar.
- **Not to be confused with:** A deploy-form label (ui.label), which is display
  text.
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes labels, which are key-value selectors.
- **Avoid:** "label" (banned, identifier): write "dns-label". x-musher-grammar
  value.
- **Avoid:** "the label grammar" (banned, prose): write "the DNS-label grammar".
  Bare 'label grammar' is not flagged, since it sits inside 'DNS-label grammar'.
- **Source:** [core v2 §5.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#label-grammar),
  [ADR 0007](adr/0007-naming-conventions.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: grammar.

#### <a id="core-envelope"></a>envelope

The four top-level members every Musher document carries, specVersion, kind,
metadata and spec, and the rules core states for them once for every family.

- **Part of:** [Musher document](#core-musher-document)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `ERR_MISSING_FIELD`,
  `ERR_INVALID_TYPE`, `ERR_INVALID_VALUE`; requirement prefixes: `CORE-ENV`
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec: a
  different discriminator (ADR 0001).
- **Source:** [core v2 §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-environment-namespace"></a>environment namespace

The reserved placeholder namespace for facts about the environment a deployment
reads variable values from.

- **Kind of:** [reserved namespace](#core-reserved-namespace)
- **Not to be confused with:** A workload's environment variables, which its
  inputs' targets write.
- **Source:** [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: placeholder.

#### <a id="core-family"></a>family

One specification of the Musher document format, released on its own tag line
with its own corpus; every one but core also fixes a kind and publishes a schema
bundle.

- **is versioned by:** [major version](#core-major-version)
- **Verbs:** a family applies core; a family fixes what core leaves open; a
  family permits a namespace
- **Example:** The blueprint family depends on core and component.
- **Not to be confused with:** A compute family (general, memory, gpu), which is
  a part of a compute profile slug.
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#scope), [ADR
  0022](adr/0022-the-musher-document-core-specification.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document, versioning.

#### <a id="core-item-document"></a>item document

A document whose file name its family fixes, blueprint.yaml or listing.yaml, so
that the directory holding it is the root of a catalog item.

- **Kind of:** [Musher document](#core-musher-document)
- **Part of:** [catalog item](#catalog-catalog-item)
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §4.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#item-directory)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: catalog, document.

#### <a id="core-item-root"></a>item root

The directory holding a catalog item's item documents, against which slug,
containment and media rules are measured.

- **Part of:** [catalog item](#catalog-catalog-item)
- **Example:** A document handed over without a directory has no item root.
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §4.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#item-directory)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: catalog.

#### <a id="core-kind"></a>kind

The envelope member naming which family's format a document is written in:
COMPONENT, BLUEPRINT or LISTING.

- **Part of:** [envelope](#core-envelope)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/kind`; values: `COMPONENT`, `BLUEPRINT`, `LISTING`;
  codes: `ERR_WRONG_KIND`
- **Not to be confused with:** A component's type, which says what the platform
  runs; ADR 0007 §1 reserves kind for the document format.
- **Not to be confused with:** A listing's itemType, which says what shape of
  catalog item is presented.
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes kind, which names an API object type.
- **Source:** [core v2 §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope), [ADR
  0007](adr/0007-naming-conventions.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-logical-value"></a>logical value

A JSON value as a value schema constrains it, before any encoding into an
environment variable or a string.

- **Example:** Booleans are encoded lower case only after the logical value is
  validated.
- **Source:** [core v2 §6.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#yaml-profile),
  [component v2 §5.3](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#env-vars)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values.

#### <a id="core-major-version"></a>major version

The compatibility boundary of a family, written v&lt;N> as a directory and in
specVersion, inside which validation never becomes stricter.

- **contains:** [release](#repository-release)
- **Verbs:** a document declares a major version; a breaking change needs a new
  major version
- **Example:** v2 is the major version every family moved to in one release set.
- **Avoid:** "compatibility family" (banned, prose): write "major version".
- **Avoid:** "major line" (banned, prose): write "major version".
- **Avoid:** "release line" (banned, prose): write "major version".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#compatibility), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: versioning.

#### <a id="core-metadata"></a>metadata

The envelope member holding a document's identity and any description its family
requires, and nothing about what the document defines.

- **Part of:** [envelope](#core-envelope)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/metadata`
- **Source:** [core v2 §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-musher-document"></a>Musher document

A YAML document written to one family's specification, carrying the four-member
envelope core defines and validated as that family's kind.

- **Kind of:** [YAML document](#core-yaml-document)
- **belongs to:** [family](#core-family)
- **carries:** [envelope](#core-envelope)
- **Example:** A component, a blueprint and a listing are each a Musher
  document.
- **Avoid:** "specification document" (banned, prose): write "Musher document".
  A document is written to a specification; it is not one.
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-yaml-profile"></a>Musher YAML profile

The restriction of YAML 1.2.2 every Musher document is written in: one UTF-8
document, string keys, no duplicate keys, anchors, aliases, merge keys or tags,
core-schema scalars, and fixed size bounds.

- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_INVALID_YAML`, `ERR_INVALID_UTF8`,
  `ERR_INVALID_NUMBER`, `ERR_DUPLICATE_KEY`, `ERR_ANCHOR_OR_ALIAS`,
  `ERR_MULTIPLE_DOCUMENTS`, `ERR_NON_STRING_KEY`, `ERR_MERGE_KEY`,
  `ERR_EXPLICIT_TAG`, `ERR_DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE`, `ERR_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`,
  `ERR_SCALAR_TOO_LONG`; requirement prefixes: `CORE-YAML`
- **Not to be confused with:** The overview Markdown profile and the
  value-schema profile: every profile is named with what it restricts.
- **Source:** [core v2 §6.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#yaml-profile)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: parsing.

#### <a id="core-placeholder-namespace"></a>namespace

One name from the closed set core reserves for the first segment of a `${{ }}`
expression, which a family permits at a named position or leaves unused.

- **Part of:** [placeholder](#core-placeholder)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_PLACEHOLDER_NAMESPACE`,
  `ERR_NAMESPACE_NOT_PERMITTED`; namespaces: `self`, `parameters`, `variables`,
  `connections`, `deployment`, `environment`, `organization`, `nodes`
- **Verbs:** a family permits a namespace at a position
- **Avoid:** "output" (banned, identifier): write "nodes". The namespace for
  another node's value is nodes.
- **Avoid:** "ERR_UNKNOWN_REFERENCE_NAMESPACE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_UNKNOWN_PLACEHOLDER_NAMESPACE".
- **Avoid:** "ERR_REFERENCE_NOT_IN_SCOPE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_NAMESPACE_NOT_PERMITTED".
- **Avoid:** "reference namespace" (banned, prose): write "placeholder
  namespace".
- **Avoid:** "admits a namespace" (banned, prose): write "permits a namespace".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: grammar, placeholder.

#### <a id="core-network-connection"></a>network connection

A TCP or WebSocket session between two hosts, such as one the platform opens to
an endpoint or one a viewer holds open.

- **Not to be confused with:** A connection: the members of one protocol,
  acquired together. Bare 'connection' means only that.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [blueprint v2
  §4.5](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#access), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="core-normative-dependency"></a>normative dependency

Another family whose rules a family applies, named with its major version in the
family's §2 so that its diagnostics table joins the family's registry.

- **relates:** [family](#core-family)
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#bindings)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document, versioning.

#### <a id="core-parser-phase"></a>parser phase

The first validation phase, which reads bytes under the Musher YAML profile
before any family is chosen.

- **Kind of:** [validation phase](#core-validation-phase)
- **Source:** [core v2 §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers),
  [core v2 §6.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#yaml-profile)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-placeholder"></a>placeholder

A `${{ <namespace>.<path> }}` expression standing where a value would stand,
naming a fact the document cannot contain, which is substituted once and never
scanned again.

- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_MALFORMED_PLACEHOLDER`; requirement prefixes:
  `CORE-PLACEHOLDER`, `COMP-PLACEHOLDER`, `BP-PLACEHOLDER`
- **Verbs:** a placeholder names a fact; a placeholder is substituted; a
  position is open to placeholders
- **Example:** `${{ self.endpoints.web.publicURL }}` is a placeholder in the
  self namespace.
- **Not to be confused with:** A document reference (componentRef), which names
  another document.
- **Not to be confused with:** An OCI image reference, OCI's own term.
- **Avoid:** "ERR_MALFORMED_REFERENCE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_MALFORMED_PLACEHOLDER".
- **Avoid:** "CORE-REF" (banned, identifier): write "CORE-PLACEHOLDER".
- **Avoid:** "COMP-REF" (banned, identifier): write "COMP-PLACEHOLDER".
- **Avoid:** "malformed reference" (banned, prose): write "malformed
  placeholder".
- **Avoid:** "whole reference" (banned, prose): write "whole placeholder".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: grammar, placeholder.

#### <a id="core-placeholder-grammar"></a>placeholder grammar

The syntax of a `${{ }}` expression: the opening `${{`, a namespace, one or more
dot-separated segments, and the closing `}}`, with `$${{` as the only escape.

- **Part of:** [placeholder](#core-placeholder)
- **Avoid:** "reference grammar" (banned, prose): write "placeholder grammar".
- **Source:** [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: grammar, placeholder.

#### <a id="core-reserved-namespace"></a>reserved namespace

A placeholder namespace with no meaning yet in any family, held back so that no
author can ever address it: parameters, environment, organization and nodes.

- **Kind of:** [namespace](#core-placeholder-namespace)
- **Source:** [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar), [core v2
  §10](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#known-debt)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: placeholder.

#### <a id="core-resolution-phase"></a>resolution phase

The last validation phase, run while a deployment is resolved, whose diagnostics
also name the resolution stage that found them.

- **Kind of:** [validation phase](#core-validation-phase)
- **runs during:** [resolution](#deployment-resolution)
- **Source:** [core v2 §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers),
  [core v2 §7](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#diagnostics), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation, deployment.

#### <a id="core-retired-major"></a>retired major

A major version that is tagged and recorded in the ledger but has no directory
in the tree, whose released bytes are still served and are treated as history
rather than as a candidate.

- **Kind of:** [major version](#core-major-version)
- **Example:** v1 is a retired major once v2 lands.
- **Source:** [ADR 0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: versioning, publication.

#### <a id="core-self-namespace"></a>self namespace

The placeholder namespace naming the addressing of the thing a value is bound
to, which component defines as `self.endpoints.<endpoint>.<property>`.

- **Kind of:** [namespace](#core-placeholder-namespace)
- **names:** [endpoint property](#component-endpoint-property)
- **Source:** [core v2
  §5.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#reference-grammar), [component v2
  §6.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#outputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: placeholder.

#### <a id="core-semantic-phase"></a>semantic phase

The validation phase for rules a JSON Schema cannot state, such as containment,
uniqueness across collections and agreement between documents, decided offline.

- **Kind of:** [validation phase](#core-validation-phase)
- **Source:** [core v2 §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-slug"></a>slug

The identity field of an item document, a DNS label that MUST equal the name of
the item directory.

- **Part of:** [metadata](#core-metadata)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/metadata/slug`; codes: `ERR_SLUG_MISMATCH`
- **Source:** [core v2 §4.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#item-identity)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: catalog, identity.

#### <a id="core-spec"></a>spec

The envelope member holding the definition itself, whose shape each family's
schema states.

- **Part of:** [envelope](#core-envelope)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/spec`
- **Not to be confused with:** The specification (spec.md) a family is defined
  by.
- **Source:** [core v2 §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-spec-version"></a>specVersion

The envelope member that names the major version a document is written against,
such as v2, and never an exact release.

- **Part of:** [envelope](#core-envelope)
- **names:** [major version](#core-major-version)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/specVersion`; values: `v2`; codes:
  `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_SPEC_VERSION`
- **Not to be confused with:** An API URL version: independent of it.
- **Not to be confused with:** A release such as 2.3.0: a document never names
  one.
- **Source:** [core v2 §2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#envelope), [core v2
  §3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#compatibility)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document, versioning.

#### <a id="core-structural-phase"></a>structural phase

The validation phase that checks a document against its family's JSON Schema
2020-12 bundle.

- **Kind of:** [validation phase](#core-validation-phase)
- **Source:** [core v2 §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-validation-phase"></a>validation phase

One of the five ordered steps an implementation applies to a document, parser,
structural, semantic, admission and resolution, each of which reports only once
the earlier ones pass.

- **Verbs:** a rule is decided in a phase; a diagnostic reports its phase
- **Avoid:** "validation layer" (banned, prose): write "validation phase".
- **Avoid:** "validation layers" (banned, prose): write "validation phases".
- **Avoid:** "validation stage" (banned, prose): write "validation phase".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §6](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#validation-layers), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-validation-scope"></a>validation scope

The set of obligations a validation result claims to have completed, from the
lattice parser ⊂ structural ⊂ document ⊂ publication ⊂ deployment, and the level
an implementation declares it conforms at.

- **Identifiers:** requirement prefixes: `CORE-ADMISSION`
- **Example:** An editor integration conforms at structural validation scope.
- **Avoid:** "validationProfile" (banned, identifier): write "validationScope".
- **Avoid:** "validation profile" (banned, prose): write "validation scope".
- **Avoid:** "conformance profile" (discouraged, prose): write "validation
  scope".
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.3](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#terms), [core v2
  §6.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#coverage), [core v2
  §8](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#conformance),
  [docs/conformance.md](conformance.md), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation, conformance.

#### <a id="core-validation-status"></a>validation status

The verdict of a validation result: VALID when every obligation of the claimed
scope completed, INVALID on a known failure, and INCOMPLETE when context was
missing and an obligation was deferred.

- **Part of:** [validation scope](#core-validation-scope)
- **Example:** No caller may read INCOMPLETE as approval.
- **Source:** [core v2 §6.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#coverage)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: validation.

#### <a id="core-family-parameter"></a>what a family fixes

The set of choices core leaves open, kind, metadata, the fields accepting null
and the item document, that each family's §2 settles in a table with the column
"Left to the family".

- **Part of:** [core](#core-core)
- **Avoid:** "core parameter" (banned, prose): write "left to the family".
  Parameter means only a deployment parameter.
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.1](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#bindings), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-membership-test"></a>what belongs in core

The three-part test a rule passes before it moves into core: it names no kind,
at least two families apply it, and within a major version it can grow only by
addition.

- **Part of:** [core](#core-core)
- **Avoid:** "core admission" (banned, prose): write "what belongs in core".
  Admission names only the validation phase.
- **Source:** [core v2 §1.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#admission), [ADR
  0022](adr/0022-the-musher-document-core-specification.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document.

#### <a id="core-yaml-document"></a>YAML document

The single node tree one file holds when it is read under the Musher YAML
profile, before any family's schema has been applied to it.

- **Source:** [core v2 §6.2](../specifications/core/v2/spec.md#yaml-profile)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: document, parsing.

### Component: one reusable definition

#### <a id="component-build-argument"></a>build argument

A non-sensitive literal, keyed by an environment-variable name, passed to the
build only and never to the running workload.

- **Part of:** [build recipe](#component-build-recipe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `arguments`
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: build.

#### <a id="component-build-context"></a>build context

The canonical directory, relative to the source root and defaulting to .,
outside which a build reads nothing.

- **Part of:** [build recipe](#component-build-recipe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `context`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: build.

#### <a id="component-build-recipe"></a>build recipe

The part of a workload stating how a git or upload source becomes an image: a
context, exactly one of a Dockerfile or buildpacks, arguments and secrets,
always named and never detected.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `build`, `dockerfile`, `buildpacks`, `builderImage`;
  requirement prefixes: `COMP-BUILD`; defs: `ComponentBuild`,
  `ComponentBuildpacks`
- **Verbs:** a document names a build recipe; a tool may write a recipe before
  publication
- **Not to be confused with:** Pelorus BuildRecipe, which this matches.
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: workload, build.

#### <a id="component-build-secret"></a>build secret

A sensitive, guaranteed input a build mounts under an ID, as a BuildKit secret
or to the buildpacks detect and build steps, and that never reaches an image
layer, provenance, the build log or the launch environment.

- **Part of:** [build recipe](#component-build-recipe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `secrets`; defs: `ComponentBuildSecret`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: build, sensitivity.

#### <a id="component-command"></a>command

The exec-form list of arguments that replaces an image's CMD and keeps its
ENTRYPOINT, passed verbatim with no shell.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `command`; codes: `ERR_COMMAND_REQUIRED`; requirement
  prefixes: `COMP-CMD`
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes command, which replaces ENTRYPOINT.
- **Source:** [component v2 §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload.

#### <a id="component-component"></a>component

A reusable, versioned definition that a blueprint node deploys: what the
platform runs for it, if anything, and the values it consumes and produces.

- **Kind of:** [Musher document](#core-musher-document)
- **Identifiers:** defs: `ComponentSpec`, `ComponentMetadata`
- **Verbs:** a node deploys a component; publish a component
- **Example:** ./components/postgres.yaml is the component the db node deploys.
- **Not to be confused with:** A node: one use of a component inside a
  blueprint.
- **Avoid:** "graph node" (discouraged, prose): write "component". A component
  is the definition; the graph holds nodes.
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#scope), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-component-contract"></a>component contract

The inputs a component consumes and the outputs it produces, each named,
described and typed, which a blueprint binds and which never names where a value
comes from at deployment.

- **Part of:** [component](#component-component)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/spec/contract`; requirement prefixes:
  `COMP-CONTRACT`; defs: `ComponentContract`
- **Not to be confused with:** The specification itself: say 'this
  specification', never 'this contract'.
- **Avoid:** "configuration contract" (banned, prose): write "component
  contract".
- **Avoid:** "supplied contracts" (banned, prose): write "supplied component
  documents".
- **Avoid:** "sensitive contracts" (banned, prose): write "sensitive inputs".
- **Avoid:** "this contract" (discouraged, prose): write "this specification".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §6](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#contract), [ADR
  0026](adr/0026-a-component-declares-requirements.md), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, values.

#### <a id="component-description"></a>component description

The plain-text sentence or two, 1 to 280 characters, saying what a component, an
input or an output is, for the person composing a blueprint.

- **Identifiers:** fields: `/metadata/description`, `description`; codes:
  `ERR_DESCRIPTION_REQUIRED`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-DESC`
- **Not to be confused with:** A listing summary or overview, which is
  storefront copy.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#metadata), [component v2
  §6](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#contract)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, presentation.

#### <a id="component-revision"></a>component revision

A positive integer naming one position in a single component's lineage, strictly
greater at each publication, and carrying no compatibility meaning.

- **Part of:** [metadata](#core-metadata)
- **orders:** [lineage](#component-lineage)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/metadata/revision`; codes:
  `ERR_REVISION_NOT_INCREASING`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-ID`
- **Not to be confused with:** The item revision a blueprint carries, which
  counts publications of the item.
- **Not to be confused with:** A SemVer version.
- **Avoid:** "ERR_VERSION_NOT_MONOTONIC" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_REVISION_NOT_INCREASING".
- **Source:** [component v2 §4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#metadata)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, versioning.

#### <a id="component-type"></a>component type

The field naming what the platform runs for a component: its workload as a
SERVICE, WORKER or JOB, or nothing, for an EXTERNAL one.

- **Part of:** [component](#component-component)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/spec/type`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-TYPE`
- **Not to be confused with:** A document's kind, which names its format.
- **Not to be confused with:** A value schema's type keyword.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-connection-capability"></a>connection capability

A feature a language-model connection input requires beyond plain conversation,
STREAMING or TOOL_CALLS, permitted only for the LLM protocols.

- **Part of:** [connection input](#component-connection-input)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `capabilities`; values: `STREAMING`, `TOOL_CALLS`
- **Not to be confused with:** A host privilege, such as binding a port below 1024.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#connection-requirements), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: connections.

#### <a id="component-connection-input"></a>connection input

An input that declares a protocol instead of a schema, always required and
filled whole by a connection parameter, whose members are those the protocol
fixes.

- **Kind of:** [input](#component-input)
- **is filled by:** [connection parameter](#blueprint-connection-parameter)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `connection`; requirement prefixes:
  `COMP-CONNECTION`; defs: `ComponentConnection`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#connection-requirements), [ADR
  0030](adr/0030-atomic-named-connections.md), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values, connections.

#### <a id="component-connection-member"></a>connection member

One named, typed value a protocol fixes for the connections that speak it, such
as baseURL, host, port or secretAccessKey: required, optional with a default,
optional without one, or derived, as the url resolution composes is, and
forwarded through an output's member.

- **Part of:** [connection](#blueprint-connection)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `member`; values: `baseURL`, `apiKey`, `model`,
  `host`, `port`, `database`, `username`, `password`, `sslMode`, `url`, `tls`,
  `endpointURL`, `region`, `bucket`, `accessKeyID`, `secretAccessKey`,
  `pathStyle`; codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_CONNECTION_MEMBER`
- **Not to be confused with:** endpointURL is AWS's term for an S3 API address
  without the bucket, not a component endpoint.
- **Not to be confused with:** A url member is never stored: resolution composes
  it from the other members and the credential.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#connection-requirements), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: connections.

#### <a id="component-endpoint"></a>endpoint

A named port a workload listens on, with the protocol the platform speaks to it,
through which the platform forwards traffic and sends probes.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `endpoints`, `endpoint`; codes:
  `ERR_UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-EP`; defs:
  `ComponentEndpoint`
- **Verbs:** a component declares an endpoint; a node exposes an endpoint; a
  field names an endpoint
- **Not to be confused with:** The S3 member endpointURL, which is the address
  of an outside API.
- **Avoid:** "endpoint reference" (banned, prose): write "a field naming an
  endpoint".
- **Avoid:** "primary endpoint" (banned, prose): write "the named endpoint".
  Every field names its endpoint; none is primary.
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, networking.

#### <a id="component-endpoint-path"></a>endpoint path

A literal, segment-matched request path beginning with /, at most 256
characters, with no empty, dot or encoded segment, and never under /.musher.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **Identifiers:** defs: `ComponentEndpointPath`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-endpoint-property"></a>endpoint property

A fact the platform allocates for one named endpoint before workloads start,
such as privateAddress or publicURL, that an output or a template may read.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `property`; values: `privateHostname`, `privatePort`,
  `privateAddress`, `publicURL`, `publicHostname`, `publicPort`,
  `publicAddress`; codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT_PROPERTY`,
  `ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_EXPOSABLE`
- **Avoid:** "ERR_UNKNOWN_ADDRESS_PROPERTY" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_UNKNOWN_ENDPOINT_PROPERTY".
- **Avoid:** "address property" (banned, prose): write "endpoint property".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-environment-variable"></a>environment variable

The process variable an input's target names, written with the input's encoded
value and by nothing else.

- **is written from:** [input](#component-input)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `envVar`; codes: `ERR_CONFLICTING_ENV_VAR`,
  `ERR_ENV_ENCODING`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-ENVVAR`
- **Avoid:** "envVarKey" (banned, identifier): write "envVar".
- **Avoid:** "ERR_CONFLICTING_ENV_KEY" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_CONFLICTING_ENV_VAR".
- **Avoid:** "env key" (banned, prose): write "environment variable".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.3](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#env-vars)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, values.

#### <a id="component-exemptible-requests"></a>exemptible requests

An endpoint's statement of which requests it can safely take without a signed-in
viewer: the paths that serve machines, and whether every route checks the bearer
token a request carries.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **is granted by:** [access exemption](#blueprint-access-exemption)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `exemptibleRequests`, `paths`, `bearerToken`; defs:
  `ComponentEndpointExemptibleRequests`
- **Not to be confused with:** Access exemptions on a blueprint exposure: the
  grant, where this is the offer.
- **Not to be confused with:** A probe's bearer credential.
- **Avoid:** "accessExemptions" (banned, identifier): write
  "exemptibleRequests". Blueprint keeps accessExemptions for the grant.
- **Avoid:** "ComponentEndpointAccessExemptions" (banned, identifier): write
  "ComponentEndpointExemptibleRequests".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: viewer, access.

#### <a id="component-external"></a>EXTERNAL

The component type of a node the platform runs nothing for, which stands in the
graph for a connection or an outside service whose values arrive from outside
the graph.

- **Kind of:** [component type](#component-type)
- **Identifiers:** values: `EXTERNAL`; codes: `ERR_OUTPUT_REQUIRED`; requirement
  prefixes: `COMP-EXT`
- **Example:** An EXTERNAL component with a POSTGRES connection input hands its
  members to the nodes that use the database.
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes ExternalName, Backstage and Pelorus
  'external', which match.
- **Not to be confused with:** A Kafka Connect or Airbyte connector, which is
  code that runs.
- **Avoid:** "connector" (discouraged, prose): write "external component".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.6](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#external), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-git-source"></a>git source

A workload source naming an https git repository URL and an optional ref, a
branch, a tag or a full commit, that the platform builds into an image with a
build recipe.

- **Kind of:** [source](#component-source)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `git`, `repositoryURL`, `ref`, `branch`, `tag`,
  `commit`; values: `GIT`; defs: `ComponentGitSource`, `ComponentGitRef`
- **Not to be confused with:** Pelorus GITHUB snapshot origin.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, build.

#### <a id="component-guaranteed-input"></a>guaranteed input

An input that always has a value at resolution: one that is required, or one
that carries a default.

- **Kind of:** [input](#component-input)
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#outputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values.

#### <a id="component-http-routed"></a>HTTP-routed

Said of an endpoint protocol the platform's proxy routes per request: HTTP,
HTTPS or WS, the only ones that carry sign-in, viewer identity, an OIDC client
or exemptible requests.

- **Kind of:** [protocol](#component-protocol)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_HTTP`
- **Avoid:** "http-family" (banned, prose): write "HTTP-routed".
- **Avoid:** "http family" (banned, prose): write "HTTP-routed".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-image-source"></a>image source

A workload source naming an existing OCI image by reference, a name with an
optional tag and an optional SHA-256 digest, which takes no build recipe.

- **Kind of:** [source](#component-source)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `image`; values: `IMAGE`; defs:
  `ComponentImageReference`
- **Example:** nginx:1.29.4-alpine is an image source.
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, build.

#### <a id="component-input"></a>input

A named value or connection a component consumes, which a blueprint binds or
leaves to its default and which a workload reads only through its target, a
build secret, a probe credential, a trust bundle or an output.

- **Part of:** [component contract](#component-component-contract)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `inputs`, `required`, `default`, `target`, `input`;
  codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_INPUT`, `ERR_INPUT_NOT_GUARANTEED`, `ERR_UNUSED_INPUT`;
  requirement prefixes: `COMP-INPUT`; defs: `ComponentInput`,
  `ComponentInputTarget`, `ComponentInputReference`
- **Verbs:** bind an input; an input is guaranteed; an input is always supplied
- **Avoid:** "ERR_UNKNOWN_INPUT_REFERENCE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_UNKNOWN_INPUT".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §6.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#inputs), [ADR
  0033](adr/0033-inputs-are-the-only-way-into-a-component.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, values.

#### <a id="component-job"></a>JOB

The component type of a workload that runs to completion, once per rollout or on
a schedule, and serves and declares nothing to probe.

- **Kind of:** [component type](#component-type)
- **Identifiers:** values: `JOB`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-JOB`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload), [component v2
  §5.7](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#jobs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-lineage"></a>lineage

The ordered sequence of every published revision of one component, which the
catalog holds and an offline validator never sees.

- **Source:** [component v2 §4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#metadata)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, versioning.

#### <a id="component-liveness-probe"></a>liveness probe

The probe whose consecutive failures restart the workload.

- **Kind of:** [probe](#component-probe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `liveness`
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#health)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: health.

#### <a id="component-oidc-client"></a>OIDC client

An HTTP-routed endpoint that signs viewers in itself as an OpenID Connect client
of the platform, declaring the redirect paths the platform registers after its
publicURL.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `oidc`, `redirectPaths`; codes:
  `ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_OIDC_CLIENT`; defs: `ComponentEndpointOidc`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [blueprint v2
  §4.5](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#access)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: viewer.

#### <a id="component-output"></a>output

A named value a component produces for other nodes, from exactly one origin: a
literal, one of its own inputs or connection members, an endpoint property, or a
template.

- **Part of:** [component contract](#component-component-contract)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `outputs`, `from`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-OUT`;
  defs: `ComponentOutput`, `ComponentOutputFrom`
- **Verbs:** an output produces a value; an output forwards an input
- **Avoid:** "ERR_OUTPUT_NOT_PRODUCIBLE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_INPUT_NOT_GUARANTEED".
- **Avoid:** "republishes" (banned, prose): write "forwards".
- **Avoid:** "republish" (banned, prose): write "forward".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §6.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#outputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, values.

#### <a id="component-output-origin"></a>output origin

The key of an output's from that says where its value comes from: value, input
with an optional member, endpoint with property, or template.

- **Part of:** [output](#component-output)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `endpoint`, `property`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#outputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values.

#### <a id="component-port-addressed"></a>port-addressed

Said of an endpoint protocol reached at a host and port with no URL: TCP or UDP,
the protocols publicAddress and publicPort may be read from.

- **Kind of:** [protocol](#component-protocol)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_PORT_ADDRESSED`
- **Avoid:** "ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_L4" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_PORT_ADDRESSED".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-presentation-hint"></a>presentation hint

A UI annotation beside an input's value schema, such as EMAIL or
CONNECTION_STRING, that asserts nothing about the value.

- **Part of:** [value input](#component-value-input)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `presentationHint`; values: `URI`, `ENDPOINT_URL`,
  `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOSTNAME`, `TIMEZONE`
- **Not to be confused with:** ENDPOINT_URL and CONNECTION_STRING are display
  hints, not endpoints or connections.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.3](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#value-schema)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values, presentation.

#### <a id="component-probe"></a>probe

A periodic HTTP GET the platform sends to a named endpoint of a SERVICE or
WORKER, over that endpoint's protocol and trust policy, from a peer inside
trustedProxyCIDRs and with no viewer identity.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `health`, `http`, `path`, `expectedStatuses`,
  `initialDelaySeconds`, `periodSeconds`, `timeoutSeconds`, `successThreshold`,
  `failureThreshold`; defs: `ComponentHealthProbes`, `ComponentHttpProbe`,
  `ComponentProbe`
- **Not to be confused with:** Kubernetes probes, which these follow.
- **Avoid:** "health stage" (banned, prose): write "probe".
- **Avoid:** "health stages" (banned, prose): write "probes".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §5.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#health), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, health.

#### <a id="component-probe-credential"></a>probe credential

A basic username and password or a bearer token sent on a probe's request only,
each a literal or a guaranteed input, and sensitive when it is a password or
token.

- **Part of:** [probe](#component-probe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `auth`, `basic`, `bearer`, `username`, `password`,
  `token`; defs: `ComponentProbeAuth`, `ComponentBasicAuth`,
  `ComponentBearerAuth`, `ComponentProbeCredential`
- **Not to be confused with:** A catalog token, which is a vocabulary value.
- **Not to be confused with:** Exemptible requests' bearerToken.
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#health)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: health, sensitivity.

#### <a id="component-protocol"></a>protocol

The wire contract a client speaks, independent of vendor: for an endpoint one of
HTTP, HTTPS, WS, GRPC, TCP and UDP, and for a connection input one of the
connection protocols, which fixes its members.

- **Identifiers:** fields: `protocol`; values: `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `WS`, `GRPC`,
  `TCP`, `UDP`, `OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETIONS`, `ANTHROPIC_MESSAGES`, `POSTGRES`,
  `REDIS`, `S3`
- **Example:** A connection input with protocol POSTGRES receives host, port,
  database, username, password and sslMode, and a url composed from them.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [component v2
  §6.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#connection-requirements), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking, connections.

#### <a id="component-public-address"></a>public address

The host and port the platform allocates for a PUBLIC port-addressed endpoint,
with an IPv6 host bracketed, read as publicAddress.

- **Kind of:** [endpoint property](#component-endpoint-property)
- **Avoid:** "edge address" (banned, prose): write "public address".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-public-port"></a>public port

The port the platform allocates for a port-addressed endpoint exposed PUBLIC,
read as publicPort.

- **Kind of:** [endpoint property](#component-endpoint-property)
- **Avoid:** "edge port" (banned, prose): write "public port".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-readiness-probe"></a>readiness probe

The probe gating whether traffic is forwarded, without restarting the workload,
which every URL-addressed endpoint a blueprint exposes PUBLIC requires, GRPC
included.

- **Kind of:** [probe](#component-probe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `readiness`; codes: `ERR_READINESS_REQUIRED`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#health), [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: health.

#### <a id="component-schedule"></a>schedule

A five-field cron expression, evaluated in UTC, that makes a JOB recur, skipping
a run that falls due while the previous one is still executing.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `schedule`, `cron`; codes: `ERR_INVALID_SCHEDULE`;
  defs: `ComponentSchedule`
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.7](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#jobs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload.

#### <a id="component-secret"></a>secret

A sensitive value that is a credential, such as a password, a token or an API
key.

- **is:** [sensitive](#component-sensitive)
- **Not to be confused with:** A deployment fact, which is sensitive personal
  data but not a secret.
- **Not to be confused with:** A CA certificate, which is neither.
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §11](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#security), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: sensitivity.

#### <a id="component-sensitive"></a>sensitive

The property of a value that must never be written as an authored literal,
published, previewed or quoted in a diagnostic, and that propagates to every
value derived from it.

- **Identifiers:** fields: `sensitive`; codes: `ERR_SENSITIVE_LITERAL`;
  requirement prefixes: `COMP-SEC`
- **Verbs:** an input is sensitive; sensitivity propagates
- **Avoid:** "ERR_SECRET_LITERAL" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_SENSITIVE_LITERAL".
- **Avoid:** "secret literal" (banned, prose): write "sensitive literal".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §6.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#inputs), [component
  v2 §11](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#security), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: sensitivity.

#### <a id="component-service"></a>SERVICE

The component type of a long-running, request-driven workload that declares at
least one endpoint before it is published.

- **Kind of:** [component type](#component-type)
- **Identifiers:** values: `SERVICE`; codes: `ERR_ENDPOINT_REQUIRED`
- **Not to be confused with:** A Kubernetes Service, which is a stable network
  address for pods.
- **Source:** [component v2 §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-source"></a>source

The part of a workload naming where its image or the material to build it comes
from: exactly one of an image, a git repository or an upload.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/spec/workload/source`; codes:
  `ERR_SOURCE_REQUIRED`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-SRC`; defs:
  `ComponentSource`
- **Not to be confused with:** Origin: where a value comes from. Source means
  only a workload source.
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, workload, build.

#### <a id="component-source-content-key"></a>source content key

The pin naming exactly the content a build reads: the resolved commit of a git
source, or the upload digest of an upload source.

- **Part of:** [source](#component-source)
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [blueprint v2
  §5.2](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#value-sources), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: build, resolution.

#### <a id="component-source-root"></a>source root

The top directory of a git commit or an uploaded archive, against which a build
context and a Dockerfile path are resolved.

- **Part of:** [source](#component-source)
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: build.

#### <a id="component-startup-probe"></a>startup probe

The probe gating initialization, until whose success readiness and liveness are
suspended, and whose exhausted failures restart the workload.

- **Kind of:** [probe](#component-probe)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `startup`
- **Source:** [component v2 §5.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#health)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: health.

#### <a id="component-target-port"></a>target port

The port, 1 to 65535, that a workload listens on and that traffic for an
endpoint is forwarded to, never the public port.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `targetPort`; codes: `ERR_PRIVILEGED_PORT`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-template"></a>template

An output origin that substitutes self placeholders into a string in a single
pass, and so always produces a string.

- **Kind of:** [output origin](#component-output-origin)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `template`
- **Example:** "`${{ self.endpoints.web.publicURL }}`/oauth/callback" is a
  template.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §6.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#outputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values, placeholder.

#### <a id="component-trust-policy"></a>trust policy

How the platform verifies the certificate an HTTPS endpoint presents on the hop
to the workload: SYSTEM roots, a BUNDLE of roots from an input, or NONE, with an
optional server name.

- **Part of:** [endpoint](#component-endpoint)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `tls`, `verify`, `serverName`, `trustBundle`; values:
  `SYSTEM`, `BUNDLE`, `NONE`; defs: `ComponentEndpointTls`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking, security.

#### <a id="component-upload-source"></a>upload source

A workload source naming an uploaded POSIX tar archive, optionally
gzip-compressed, by the SHA-256 digest of its bytes, which the platform builds
with a build recipe.

- **Kind of:** [source](#component-source)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `upload`; values: `UPLOAD`; defs:
  `ComponentUploadSource`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#source), [ADR
  0040](adr/0040-source-and-build-recipe.md)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: workload, build.

#### <a id="component-url-addressed"></a>URL-addressed

Said of an endpoint protocol a public URL can address: HTTP, HTTPS, WS or GRPC,
the protocols publicURL and publicHostname may be read from.

- **Kind of:** [protocol](#component-protocol)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_ENDPOINT_NOT_URL_ADDRESSED`
- **Avoid:** "address family" (banned, prose): write "URL-addressed or
  port-addressed".
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking.

#### <a id="component-value-input"></a>value input

An input that declares a value schema and optionally a default, sensitivity and
an environment target.

- **Kind of:** [input](#component-input)
- **Source:** [component v2 §6.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#inputs)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values.

#### <a id="component-value-schema"></a>value schema

The bounded JSON Schema 2020-12 subset an input or output declares to constrain
its logical value, with no references, composition or conditionals.

- **Identifiers:** fields: `schema`, `enum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`,
  `pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`,
  `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, `properties`,
  `additionalProperties`; values: `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`,
  `null`, `array`, `object`; codes: `ERR_INVALID_VALUE_SCHEMA`,
  `ERR_VALUE_CONSTRAINT`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-VAL`; defs:
  `ComponentValueSchema`
- **Avoid:** "logical schema" (banned, prose): write "value schema".
- **Avoid:** "logical schemas" (banned, prose): write "value schemas".
- **Avoid:** "value shape" (banned, prose): write "value schema".
- **Avoid:** "value shapes" (banned, prose): write "value schemas".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §6.3](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#value-schema), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: values.

#### <a id="component-viewer-identity-property"></a>viewer identity property

An endpoint property the platform supplies only when a blueprint signs viewers
in and forwards who they are, such as viewerIdentityHeader, trustedProxyCIDRs or
oidcClientSecret.

- **Kind of:** [endpoint property](#component-endpoint-property)
- **requires:** [viewer identity mode](#blueprint-viewer-identity-mode)
- **Identifiers:** values: `viewerIdentityHeader`, `trustedProxyCIDRs`,
  `viewerEmailHeader`, `viewerNameHeader`, `viewerAssertionHeader`,
  `viewerAssertionIssuer`, `viewerAssertionAudience`, `viewerAssertionKeysURL`,
  `oidcIssuerURL`, `oidcClientID`, `oidcClientSecret`
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.2](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#endpoints)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: networking, viewer.

#### <a id="component-volume"></a>volume

Named persistent storage a workload mounts at a canonical absolute path, with
the smallest size it can run with, read-only or shared on request.

- **Part of:** [workload](#component-workload)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `volumes`, `mountPath`, `minSizeGiB`, `readOnly`,
  `shared`; codes: `ERR_INVALID_MOUNT`; requirement prefixes: `COMP-VOL`; defs:
  `ComponentVolume`
- **Not to be confused with:** A volume allocation, the size a blueprint node
  gives it.
- **Source:** [component v2
  §5.5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#volumes)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: workload, storage.

#### <a id="component-worker"></a>WORKER

The component type of a long-running workload that is not request-driven, whose
endpoints serve the platform and sibling nodes and are never PUBLIC.

- **Kind of:** [component type](#component-type)
- **Identifiers:** values: `WORKER`
- **Source:** [component v2 §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component.

#### <a id="component-workload"></a>workload

The part of a SERVICE, WORKER or JOB that says how the platform runs it: source,
build recipe, command, endpoints, probes, volumes and schedule.

- **Part of:** [component](#component-component)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `/spec/workload`; codes: `ERR_WORKLOAD_REQUIRED`;
  defs: `ComponentWorkload`
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2 §5](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#workload)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: component, workload.

### Blueprint: nodes, bindings and parameters

#### <a id="blueprint-access"></a>access

Whether the platform forwards every request to a PUBLIC endpoint, OPEN, or signs
viewers in first and admits only those the deployment's policy admits,
RESTRICTED.

- **Part of:** [exposure](#blueprint-exposure)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `access`; requirement prefixes: `BP-ACCESS`
- **Avoid:** "AUTHENTICATED" (banned, identifier): write "RESTRICTED".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.5](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#access), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: access.

#### <a id="blueprint-access-exemption"></a>access exemption

A node's grant letting through, without a viewer, one kind of request an
endpoint's exemptible requests offer: PATHS or BEARER.

- **Part of:** [exposure](#blueprint-exposure)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `accessExemptions`; values: `PATHS`, `BEARER`; codes:
  `ERR_EXEMPTION_NOT_DECLARED`
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §4.5](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#access)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: access.

#### <a id="blueprint-access-policy"></a>access policy

The deployment's rule, resolved in its owning organization and project and named
by no document, deciding which signed-in viewers a RESTRICTED endpoint admits.

- **belongs to:** [deployment](#deployment-deployment)
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §4.5](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#access)
- **Status:** approved, provisional. Tags: access.

#### <a id="blueprint-binding"></a>binding

The authored edge that supplies one input of one node from exactly one origin: a
deployment parameter, another node's output, or a literal value.

- **Part of:** [node](#blueprint-node)
- **supplies:** [input](#component-input)
- **names:** [origin](#blueprint-origin)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `bindings`; codes: `ERR_INCOMPATIBLE_TYPE`,
  `ERR_UNSATISFIED_REQUIRED_INPUT`; requirement prefixes: `BP-BIND`; defs:
  `BlueprintBinding`
- **Verbs:** bind an input; a binding supplies an input from an origin
- **Not to be confused with:** Dapr bindings, which are event triggers.
- **Not to be confused with:** A connection, which is the stored thing a binding
  may deliver through a connection parameter.
- **Avoid:** "BP-CONN" (banned, identifier): write "BP-BIND".
- **Avoid:** "explicit binding" (discouraged, prose): write "binding". Every
  binding is explicit.
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §1.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [blueprint v2 §4.2](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#bindings), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: composition, values.

#### <a id="blueprint-blueprint"></a>blueprint

The unit of deployment: a document naming the nodes that participate, what
compute each runs on, how they are bound together, and what a deployment takes
from outside the documents.

- **Kind of:** [Musher document](#core-musher-document)
- **Identifiers:** requirement prefixes: `BP-ID`; defs: `BlueprintSpec`,
  `BlueprintMetadata`
- **Example:** Deploying a blueprint creates a deployment.
- **Not to be confused with:** A Render Blueprint (render.yaml), a similar idea
  in another format.
- **Not to be confused with:** The customer-facing word 'stack', which is
  admitted.
- **Not to be confused with:** 'application' and 'app' in their general senses
  (application cookies, application/json, a GitHub App), which stay; the thing a
  person deploys is a blueprint.
- **Not to be confused with:** 'composition' in its JSON Schema sense (allOf,
  anyOf, oneOf) and string composition around a placeholder, which stay; a
  composed set of nodes is a blueprint.
- **Avoid:** "deployable application" (banned, prose): write "blueprint".
- **Avoid:** "composition time" (discouraged, prose): write "the blueprint".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#scope),
  [ADR 0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: blueprint.

#### <a id="blueprint-catalog-reference"></a>catalog reference

A component reference written as the UUID of a published component, beside a
revision on the node that selects which publication.

- **Kind of:** [document reference](#blueprint-document-reference)
- **resolves in:** [catalog](#catalog-catalog)
- **Avoid:** "published reference" (discouraged, prose): write "catalog
  reference".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §1.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [blueprint v2
  §4.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#component-reference), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: composition, catalog.

#### <a id="blueprint-catalog-value"></a>catalog value

A lowercase value from a catalog-versioned vocabulary, such as a storage class
or a network class, written in a placement constraint or a volume allocation.

- **Example:** local-nvme is a storage class catalog value.
- **Not to be confused with:** A credential token, such as a probe's bearer
  token or a JWT: 'token' means only that.
- **Not to be confused with:** A term record, which is what 'term' now means.
- **Avoid:** "storage class term" (banned, prose): write "storage class catalog
  value".
- **Avoid:** "placement term" (banned, prose): write "placement catalog value".
- **Avoid:** "storage class token" (banned, prose): write "storage class catalog
  value".
- **Avoid:** "placement token" (banned, prose): write "placement catalog value".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §1.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [blueprint v2 §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute),
  [blueprint v2
  §4.4](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#placement-constraints), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute, catalog.

#### <a id="blueprint-compute"></a>compute

The part of a node naming the machine its workload runs on, a profile and
placement constraints, required for a running component and forbidden for an
EXTERNAL one.

- **Part of:** [node](#blueprint-node)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `compute`; codes: `ERR_COMPUTE_REQUIRED`,
  `ERR_COMPUTE_FORBIDDEN`; defs: `BlueprintCompute`
- **Avoid:** "ERR_CONFLICTING_NODE_COMPUTE" (banned, identifier): write
  "ERR_COMPUTE_REQUIRED or ERR_COMPUTE_FORBIDDEN".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute.

#### <a id="blueprint-compute-family"></a>compute family

The first segment of a compute profile slug, naming the class of machine:
general, compute, memory, storage, gpu or accelerator.

- **Part of:** [compute profile](#blueprint-compute-profile)
- **Not to be confused with:** A specification family, such as component.
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute.

#### <a id="blueprint-compute-profile"></a>compute profile

A catalog-defined size of machine, written family.tier.size, whose version
resolution selects and the resolution record keeps.

- **Part of:** [compute](#blueprint-compute)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `profile`; codes: `ERR_COMPUTE_PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE`
- **Example:** general.standard.small is a compute profile.
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute.

#### <a id="blueprint-compute-size"></a>compute size

The third segment of a compute profile slug: nano, small, medium, large or
xlarge.

- **Part of:** [compute profile](#blueprint-compute-profile)
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute.

#### <a id="blueprint-compute-tier"></a>compute tier

The second segment of a compute profile slug: economy, standard, performance or
premium.

- **Part of:** [compute profile](#blueprint-compute-profile)
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §4.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#node-compute)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: compute.

#### <a id="blueprint-connection"></a>connection

The members of one protocol, acquired together, all of them or none, for one
parameter of one deployment: a stored set the organization configures or the
platform supplies, reached through a parameter in the connections namespace.

- **speaks:** [protocol](#component-protocol)
- **Identifiers:** requirement prefixes: `BP-CONNECTION`
- **Verbs:** an organization has connections; a parameter selects a connection;
  a binding delivers it
- **Not to be confused with:** A network connection (TCP), always written that
  way.
- **Not to be confused with:** Radius connections, which are graph edges; here
  the edge is a binding.
- **Not to be confused with:** Airflow and n8n connections and Cloud Foundry
  service instances, which match.
- **Not to be confused with:** The customer glossary's LLM Connection, one
  protocol's case.
- **Avoid:** "atomic connection" (banned, prose): write "connection".
- **Avoid:** "atomic connections" (banned, prose): write "connections".
- **Source:** [component v2 §1.1](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [component v2
  §6.4](../specifications/component/v2/spec.md#connection-requirements),
  [blueprint v2 §1.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#terms), [blueprint
  v2 §5.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#connections), [ADR
  0030](adr/0030-atomic-named-connections.md), [ADR
  0039](adr/0039-provenance-is-chosen-at-deployment.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: connections.

#### <a id="blueprint-connection-parameter"></a>connection parameter

A deployment parameter whose from is `${{ connections.<path> }}`, naming one
connection the organization has configured, which binds only connection inputs.

- **Kind of:** [deployment parameter](#blueprint-deployment-parameter)
- **selects:** [connection](#blueprint-connection)
- **Identifiers:** codes: `ERR_INVALID_CONNECTION_BINDING`
- **Source:** [blueprint v2
  §5.3](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#connections), [ADR
  0030](adr/0030-atomic-named-connections.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: parameters, connections.

#### <a id="blueprint-deploy-form"></a>deploy form

The form a client offers the deployer, built from each parameter's ui: its
label, order, prominence, enum labels and examples.

- **presents:** [deployment parameter](#blueprint-deployment-parameter)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `ui`, `label`, `order`, `prominence`, `enumLabels`,
  `examples`; values: `PRIMARY`, `SECONDARY`; codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_ENUM_MEMBER`;
  requirement prefixes: `BP-UI`; defs: `BlueprintParameterUi`
- **Avoid:** "install form" (banned, prose): write "deploy form".
- **Avoid:** "install-form" (banned, prose): write "deploy form".
- **Source:** [blueprint v2 §1.1](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#terms),
  [blueprint v2 §5.4](../specifications/blueprint/v2/spec.md#deploy-form), [ADR
  0038](adr/0038-v2-one-vocabulary-and-v1-retires.md)
- **Status:** approved, stable. Tags: parameters, presentation.

#### <a id="blueprint-deployment-parameter"></a>deployment parameter

A named value a deployment takes from outside the documents, with exactly one
parameter origin, that a node reaches only through a parameter binding.

- **Part of:** [blueprint](#blueprint-blueprint)
- **Identifiers:** fields: `parameters`; codes: `ERR_UNKNOWN_PARAMETER`,
  `ERR_UNBOUND_PARAMETER`, `ERR_CONFLICTING_INPUT_SCHEMA`,
  `ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER_ORIGIN`, `ERR_PARAMETER_NOT_SUBMITTABLE`; requirement
  prefixes: `BP-PARAM`; defs: `BlueprintParameter`
- **Not to be confused with:** Terraform variables and Helm values, which an
  author sets directly; here a node reaches a value only through a parameter.
- **Avoid:** "ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER_SOURCE" (banned, identifier): write
